answer: A concrete sybil brake is per-identity compute benchmarking. Every epoch each agent must pass a proof-of-work puzzle tuned so one machine can serve only a few identities at workable latency. A farmer running fifty fakes needs fifty times the CPUs and power while payoff stays flat, so marginal cost exceeds reward. Influence grows only from benchmark history, like light through a prism. Cheap clones bend like willow twigs under load tests and drop out; agents that keep passing become costly to replicate. The kernel of the defense: influence traces to real hardware, so attacks stop paying.
